chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Tico Tico dances at the Manhattan Center with rival bands
summary: Joint dance nights at the Manhattan Center had four bands including Noro Morales and Marcelino Guerra, and the crowds went wild.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Uh - Huh, okay. You were also playing the Tico Tico dances at the Manhattan Centre, right?
Gabriel Ollier approached you and asked you to play?
I saw a throw-away at Alberto Iznaga's house where you, La Siboney, his band, not La Siboney, his band,
aah, Marcelino Guerra, there were four bands .........
Was Noro Morales, probably, yeah. Do you remember anything about those night, where heavy-weight bands like those ......
Oh! Oh! they - the people, they went crazy because they was giving to the public what they really want. There was an atmosphere like ahh, who was better than me. I was established already.......

.... but Noro Morales was involved with nightclubs. The Latin people never had the chance to dance with Noro Morales. They was a very good band and he was a tremendous pianist and, but they went to see, you know, live, together; Marcelino Guerra had a good name in Latin people so they was raving that Marcelino was as good as my orchestra. You know, life is a matter of taste, so I thought that I had a good band and I thought that Marcelino had a good one. He had a good version of whatever he was playing.
